math.title: School Mathematics
math.description: The most important topics from school mathematics

list.title: Natural Numbers
list.description: The numbers we count with.

list.title: Integers
list.description: The natural numbers, zero and their opposites.

list.title: Rational Numbers
list.description: Numbers that can be written as a quotient of two integers.
list.formula: ℚ = { a/b | a, b ∈ ℤ, b ≠ 0 }

list.title: Real Numbers
list.description: All rational and irrational numbers — the points on the number line.

list.title: Fractions
list.description: A notation a/b showing how many parts of a whole we take.

list.title: Decimals
list.description: Numbers written with a decimal point, by powers of ten.

list.title: Percentages
list.description: A part of a hundred: 1% is one hundredth of the whole.

list.title: Absolute Value
list.description: The distance of a number from zero — never negative.

list.title: Order of Operations
list.description: The order in which operations in an expression are carried out.
list.formula: brackets → powers and roots → × and ÷ → + and −

list.title: Powers
list.description: A short way to write repeated multiplication of the same number.
list.formula: aⁿ = a · a · … · a (n times); aᵐ · aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ

list.title: Roots
list.description: The operation that reverses raising to a power.

list.title: Scientific Notation
list.description: A way to write very large or very small numbers using a power of ten.

themes.title: Arithmetic
themes.description: Basic mathematical operations and number properties.
themes.formula: a + b = b + a; a · b = b · a

list.title: Addition
list.description: Combining two or more numbers into a sum.

list.title: Subtraction
list.description: The inverse of addition — it finds the difference.
list.formula: a − b = c ⟺ c + b = a

list.title: Multiplication
list.description: Repeated addition of equal addends.

list.title: Division
list.description: The inverse of multiplication.
list.formula: a ÷ b = c ⟺ c · b = a, b ≠ 0

list.title: Divisibility
list.description: A number is divisible by another when the remainder is zero.
list.formula: b | a ⟺ a = b · k, k ∈ ℤ

list.title: Prime Numbers
list.description: Numbers greater than 1 divisible only by 1 and themselves.

list.title: Factors
list.description: The numbers that divide a given number without a remainder.
list.formula: d | a ⟺ a = d · k, k ∈ ℤ

list.title: Multiples
list.description: The numbers obtained by multiplying a given number by an integer.

list.title: Greatest Common Divisor
list.description: The largest number that divides all of the given numbers.
list.formula: GCD(a, b) · LCM(a, b) = a · b

list.title: Least Common Multiple
list.description: The smallest positive number that is a multiple of all the given numbers.
list.formula: LCM(a, b) = a · b / GCD(a, b)

list.title: Ratios
list.description: A comparison of two quantities by division.

list.title: Proportions
list.description: An equality between two ratios.
list.formula: a : b = c : d ⟺ a · d = b · c

themes.title: Algebra
themes.description: Expressions, equations, inequalities and algebraic structures.

list.title: Variables
list.description: A letter standing for an unknown or changing number.

list.title: Algebraic Expressions
list.description: A combination of numbers, variables and operations.

list.title: Simplifying Expressions
list.description: Rewriting an expression in a shorter but equal form.

list.title: Linear Equations
list.description: An equation of the first degree in the unknown.

list.title: Quadratic Equations
list.description: An equation of the second degree in the unknown.

list.title: Systems of Equations
list.description: Several equations with shared unknowns, solved together.
list.formula: { a₁x + b₁y = c₁ ; a₂x + b₂y = c₂ }

list.title: Inequalities
list.description: A comparison of expressions using <, >, ≤ or ≥.
list.formula: a < b ⟹ a + c < b + c; multiplying by a negative number flips the sign

list.title: Polynomials
list.description: A sum of terms with whole-number powers of a variable.

list.title: Factorization
list.description: Writing an expression as a product of factors.

list.title: Algebraic Identities
list.description: Equalities that hold for every value of the variables.

list.title: Sequences
list.description: Numbers listed in order according to a rule.

list.title: Arithmetic Sequence
list.description: A sequence in which the difference between consecutive terms is constant.

list.title: Geometric Sequence
list.description: A sequence in which the ratio of consecutive terms is constant.
list.formula: aₙ = a₁ · qⁿ⁻¹; Sₙ = a₁(qⁿ − 1)/(q − 1), q ≠ 1

list.title: Function
list.description: A rule that assigns exactly one y to every x.

list.title: Domain
list.description: The set of all allowed values of x.

list.title: Range
list.description: The set of all values the function takes.

list.title: Linear Function
list.description: A function whose graph is a straight line.

list.title: Quadratic Function
list.description: A second-degree function whose graph is a parabola.
list.formula: y = ax² + bx + c; vertex at x₀ = −b/(2a)

list.title: Exponential Function
list.description: A function in which the variable is the exponent.

list.title: Graph
list.description: The set of points (x; f(x)) in the coordinate plane.

list.title: Slope
list.description: A number showing how steeply a line rises or falls.

list.title: Intercept
list.description: A point where the graph crosses an axis.

list.title: Zeros of a Function
list.description: The values of x for which the function equals zero.

themes.title: Geometry
themes.description: Shapes, angles, measurements and geometric properties.

list.title: Points
list.description: A basic idea in geometry — a position with no size.
list.formula: A ∈ a (point A lies on line a)

list.title: Lines
list.description: An endlessly long straight line determined by two points.

list.title: Line Segments
list.description: The part of a line between two points.
list.formula: |AB| = the distance between A and B

list.title: Angles
list.description: A figure formed by two rays with a common endpoint.

list.title: Triangles
list.description: A figure with three vertices, three sides and three angles.

list.title: Quadrilaterals
list.description: A figure with four vertices and four sides.

list.title: Polygons
list.description: A closed figure made of n line segments.

list.title: Circles
list.description: The points of a plane at an equal distance from a centre.

list.title: Perimeter
list.description: The total length of the sides of a figure.

list.title: Area
list.description: A measure of how much of the plane a figure covers.

list.title: Volume
list.description: A measure of the space a solid occupies.

list.title: Congruence
list.description: Figures with the same shape and the same size.

list.title: Similarity
list.description: Figures with the same shape and proportional sides.

list.title: Symmetry
list.description: A figure maps onto itself under a reflection or a rotation.
list.formula: reflection: the axis is the perpendicular bisector of AA′

themes.title: Golden Ratio
themes.description: The special proportion φ ≈ 1.618 that appears in geometry, nature, and art.

list.title: What Is the Golden Ratio?
list.description: A line cut so that the whole is to the larger part as the larger is to the smaller.

list.title: The Golden Rectangle
list.description: A rectangle whose sides are in the ratio φ : 1 and whose layout repeats after a square is cut off.

list.title: The Golden Spiral
list.description: A spiral built from quarter-circles inside nested squares that grow by a factor of φ.

list.title: Fibonacci Numbers
list.description: The sequence whose ratios approach φ as the numbers grow.

list.title: The Golden Ratio in a Face
list.description: Artists use φ to guide the placement of key facial features in portraits.

list.title: Composition in Painting
list.description: Dividing a canvas by φ gives strong lines for placing the focal elements.
list.formula: width ÷ φ marks the strong line

list.title: The Golden Triangle
list.description: An isosceles triangle with angles 36°, 72°, and 72° whose equal sides are in golden ratio to the base.

list.title: The Number φ
list.description: The positive solution to x² = x + 1, also written as (1 + √5) / 2.

list.title: The Golden Angle
list.description: A full turn split in the golden ratio gives an angle of about 137.5°.

list.title: Equilateral Triangle
list.description: A triangle with three equal sides and three 60° angles.

list.title: Isosceles Triangle
list.description: A triangle with two equal sides and equal base angles.

list.title: Scalene Triangle
list.description: A triangle whose three sides all have different lengths.

list.title: Right Triangle
list.description: A triangle with one right angle.
list.formula: a² + b² = c²; A = a · b/2

list.title: Pythagorean Theorem
list.description: The squares of the legs add up to the square of the hypotenuse.

list.title: Triangle Inequality
list.description: Each side is shorter than the sum of the other two.

list.title: Altitude
list.description: A perpendicular from a vertex to the opposite side.

list.title: Median
list.description: A segment from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side.

list.title: Angle Bisector
list.description: A ray that splits an angle into two equal parts.

list.title: Square
list.description: A quadrilateral with four equal sides and four right angles.

list.title: Rectangle
list.description: A quadrilateral with four right angles.

list.title: Parallelogram
list.description: A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides.

list.title: Rhombus
list.description: A parallelogram with four equal sides.

list.title: Trapezoid
list.description: A quadrilateral with a pair of parallel sides.

list.title: Kite
list.description: A quadrilateral with two pairs of adjacent equal sides.

list.title: Radius
list.description: A segment from the centre to a point on the circle.

list.title: Diameter
list.description: A chord through the centre — the longest chord.

list.title: Circumference
list.description: The distance all the way around the circle.

list.title: Area
list.description: The area of the disc enclosed by the circle.

list.title: Arc
list.description: A part of the circle between two of its points.

list.title: Chord
list.description: A segment joining two points on the circle.

list.title: Central Angle
list.description: An angle with its vertex at the centre of the circle.
list.formula: α = 2β (β is the inscribed angle on the same arc)

list.title: Inscribed Angle
list.description: An angle with its vertex on the circle.

list.title: Pi
list.description: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.

list.title: Cube
list.description: A solid with six equal square faces.

list.title: Cuboid
list.description: A solid with six rectangular faces.
list.formula: V = a · b · c; S = 2(ab + bc + ca)

list.title: Prism
list.description: A solid with two equal parallel bases and flat side faces.
list.formula: V = B · h; S = 2B + P · h

list.title: Pyramid
list.description: A solid with a polygon base and a single apex.

list.title: Cylinder
list.description: A solid with two equal circular bases.

list.title: Cone
list.description: A solid with a circular base and a single apex.

list.title: Sphere
list.description: The points in space at an equal distance from a centre.

list.title: Surface Area
list.description: The total area of all the faces of a solid.

list.title: Volume
list.description: A measure of the space a solid occupies.

list.title: Coordinate Plane
list.description: A plane with two perpendicular axes and an origin O.

list.title: x-axis
list.description: The horizontal axis of the coordinate plane.

list.title: y-axis
list.description: The vertical axis of the coordinate plane.

list.title: Coordinates
list.description: A pair of numbers giving the position of a point.

list.title: Distance Between Points
list.description: The length of the segment joining two points.

list.title: Midpoint
list.description: The point that divides a segment into two equal parts.

list.title: Slope
list.description: A measure of how steep a line is.

list.title: Equation of a Line
list.description: The relation between x and y for every point on the line.
list.formula: y = kx + b; ax + by + c = 0

list.title: Sine
list.description: The ratio of the opposite leg to the hypotenuse.

list.title: Cosine
list.description: The ratio of the adjacent leg to the hypotenuse.

list.title: Tangent
list.description: The ratio of the opposite leg to the adjacent leg.
list.formula: tan α = a/b = sin α / cos α

list.title: Cotangent
list.description: The reciprocal of the tangent.

list.title: Trigonometric Ratios
list.description: The ratios that link an angle to the sides of a right triangle.
list.formula: sin α = a/c; cos α = b/c; tan α = a/b

list.title: Unit Circle
list.description: A circle of radius 1 centred at the origin.
list.formula: x² + y² = 1; P(cos α; sin α)

list.title: Trigonometric Identities
list.description: Equalities that hold for every allowed angle.

list.title: Law of Sines
list.description: The sides are proportional to the sines of the opposite angles.
list.formula: a/sin α = b/sin β = c/sin γ = 2R

list.title: Law of Cosines
list.description: A generalisation of the Pythagorean theorem for any triangle.

list.title: Data
list.description: The collected values that are organised and analysed.

list.title: Mean
list.description: The sum of the values divided by how many there are.

list.title: Median
list.description: The middle value of the data once it is ordered.
list.formula: Me = the middle term of the ordered list

list.title: Mode
list.description: The value that occurs most often.
list.formula: Mo = the value with the highest frequency

list.title: Range
list.description: The difference between the largest and the smallest value.

list.title: Frequency
list.description: How many times a value occurs in the data.

list.title: Charts
list.description: A picture that shows the data visually.

list.title: Histogram
list.description: A bar chart for data grouped into intervals.
list.formula: bar height = frequency of the interval

list.title: Probability
list.description: A number between 0 and 1 measuring how likely an event is.

list.title: Outcome
list.description: One possible result of an experiment.

list.title: Event
list.description: A set of outcomes we are interested in.

list.title: Sample Space
list.description: The set of all possible outcomes of an experiment.

list.title: Independent Events
list.description: Events where one happening does not affect the other.

list.title: Conditional Probability
list.description: The probability of A given that B has happened.

themes.title: Introduction to Calculus
themes.description: Basic concepts of limits, derivatives and integrals.

list.title: Limits
list.description: The value a function approaches as x approaches a given number.

list.title: Derivatives
list.description: The branch of calculus that studies rates of change.

list.title: Derivative
list.description: The limit of the change in the function over the change in x.

list.title: Integrals
list.description: The branch of calculus that adds up infinitely small parts.

list.title: Integral
list.description: The operation that reverses differentiation.
list.formula: ∫ f(x) dx = F(x) + C, where F′(x) = f(x)

list.title: Rate of Change
list.description: How fast one quantity changes with respect to another.

list.title: Area Under the Curve
list.description: The area between the graph of a function and the x-axis.

list.title: Statement
list.description: A sentence that is either true or false.

list.title: Proof
list.description: A chain of logical steps that establishes a statement.

list.title: Theorem
list.description: An important statement that has been proved.

list.title: Lemma
list.description: A helper statement used in proving a theorem.

list.title: Corollary
list.description: A statement that follows immediately from a proved theorem.

list.title: Direct Proof
list.description: Starts from the assumption and reaches the conclusion step by step.

list.title: Proof by Contradiction
list.description: Assumes the opposite and derives a contradiction.

list.title: Mathematical Induction
list.description: A method for proving a statement for all natural numbers.
list.formula: P(1) and (P(n) ⇒ P(n + 1)) ⟹ P(n) for every n

list.title: Length
list.description: A quantity measured with the metre and its related units.

list.title: Mass
list.description: A quantity measured with grams, kilograms and tonnes.

list.title: Time
list.description: A quantity measured in seconds, minutes and hours.

list.title: Area
list.description: A quantity measured in square units.

list.title: Volume
list.description: A quantity measured in cubic units and litres.

list.title: Speed
list.description: The distance travelled per unit of time.

list.title: Temperature
list.description: A quantity measured in degrees Celsius or in kelvins.

list.title: Word Problems
list.description: Problems given in words that must be translated into mathematics.

list.title: Step by Step
list.description: Breaking the solution into small steps in order.

list.title: Known Values
list.description: The numbers and conditions the problem gives you.

list.title: Unknown Value
list.description: The quantity the problem asks you to find.

list.title: Formula
list.description: A short way to write the relation between quantities.

list.title: Solution
list.description: Carrying out the calculations according to your plan.
list.formula: substitute into the formula and compute

list.title: Answer
list.description: The final result, written with its unit.

list.title: Check
list.description: Testing whether the result really fits the conditions.
list.formula: substitute back: left side = right side
